## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A seven-*juan* late-Míng running commentary on the Lotus Sūtra by Ǒuyì Zhìxù 蕅益智旭 (1599–1655). The work is the longer companion to Zhìxù's synoptic *Lúnguàn* ([KR6d0081](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0081)): the *Lúnguàn* providing the unifying synoptic framework, the *Huìyì* providing the comprehensive running commentary on the entire Lotus.

**Abstract**

The *Huìyì* is the principal late-Míng Tiāntái-school running commentary on the Lotus Sūtra. Where [智顗](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%99%BA%E9%A1%97) Zhìyǐ's *Wénjù* ([KR6d0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0014)) and [湛然](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B9%9B%E7%84%B6) Zhànrán's *Wénjù jì* ([KR6d0015](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0015)) had established the foundational Tiāntái commentarial apparatus, Zhìxù's *Huìyì* provides the late-Míng synthetic re-presentation of that apparatus suitable for late-imperial monastic and lay readership. The work draws on (1) the foundational Tiāntái commentarial corpus; (2) the Sòng *shānjiā* tradition through Sìmíng [知禮](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%9F%A5%E7%A6%AE) Zhīlǐ; (3) Hānshān [德清](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BE%B7%E6%B8%85) Déqīng's Chán-Yogācāra synthetic apparatus; and (4) Zhìxù's own Pure Land devotional commitments.

The work's distinctive contribution is its harmonisation of the strict Tiāntái scholastic apparatus with the Pure Land devotional tradition that Zhìxù championed. The result is the principal late-Míng Tiāntái-Pure Land synthetic Lotus Sūtra commentary and one of the most influential late-imperial Buddhist commentaries on any Mahāyāna sūtra.

The composition is bracketed within Zhìxù's mature productive period after 1641, when he established his retreat at Mount Jiǔhuá 九華 and committed to systematic Tiāntái-Pure Land synthetic exposition. Most plausibly placed in the period 1645–1655.
